title: The eco-consumer’s paradox: an unusually eco-friendly item can make high-impact sequences appear worse
titleZh: 生态消费者的悖论：一件异常环保的物品会让高影响序列显得更差
abstract: Abstract The environmental impact of everyday behaviors accumulates across time. How are individual behaviors integrated when people judge their combined environmental-friendliness? In three pre-registered experiments, we found that participants perceive a sequence as more environmentally friendly when an environmentally friendly item is added, but only if the sequence has a moderate-average environmental impact (d > 1). If the sequence has a high-average environmental impact (and is sufficiently long), the unusually eco-friendly item instead leads to a downshift in perceived environmental-friendliness of the whole sequence ( d > 0.45)—a contrast effect. The results are consistent with an account in which evaluations of individual items are made retrospectively, in relation to a mental representation of the sequence as a whole. Within this account, an unusually environmentally friendly item may produce a contrast effect when it is perceived as distinct from the other items in the sequence, shifting the overall evaluation in the opposite direction.
summaryZh: 在中等平均环境影响的序列中加入环保物品会提高整体环境友好性评价，效应量 d 大于 1。 在高平均环境影响且序列足够长时，加入异常环保物品反而使整体环境友好性评价下降，呈对比效应，效应量 d 大于 0.45。 结果与一种解释一致：个体项目评价是回溯性做出的，并参照序列整体的心理表征；当异常环保物品被视为与其他项目不同时，可能产生对比效应。
